AST-aware code search for TypeScript and JavaScript.
Built for AI coding agents, not humans reading a terminal.

> **Status: early.** `monokl search` works today for TypeScript and JavaScript. Symbol lookup, references, definitions and dependents are designed (see [`docs/spec/`](docs/spec/README.md)) but not built yet. --- ## What you get Grep finds text. Embeddings find _vibes_. monokl parses your code with a compiler-grade parser ([OXC](https://oxc.rs)), so a search returns the **function, class, interface or type** that matches, not a line number to open and read. - **Whole code units, best first.** Results are ranked, with functions, classes and methods ahead of imports and re-exports. A search for `format price` puts `formatCurrency` and `validatePrice` first, because names are split on `camelCase`, `snake_case` and acronyms before matching. - **A small query language.** Plain words, `"quoted phrases"`, `+required` and `-excluded` terms, and `regex:` patterns. See [Writing a query](#writing-a-query). - **Your project's rules apply.** Files that `.gitignore` or `.ignore` exclude, hidden files, test files and binary files are skipped by default, and each has a flag to include it. - **Output sized for an agent's context.** Results are a compact table with paths relative to where you ran it, capped at 50 results, 20,000 tokens and 2 MiB by default. When something is cut, the output says how many more matched and suggests narrowing the query. - **Predictable.** The same search on the same files gives the same output, in the same order, every time. A bad pattern fails the whole search with a clear error instead of being quietly dropped. - **Hard to break.** A file with syntax errors is searched for whatever parsed. A pathologically deep file is skipped instead of crashing the search. An unreadable directory doesn't stop the rest of the search. ## Try it monokl isn't on crates.io yet; build it from source: ``` cargo build --release ``` Then search a directory (the default is the current one): ``` $ monokl search "format price" src/ --max-results 3 search[3]{file,lineStart,lineEnd,nodeKind,symbolSignature,rank,finalScore}: src/utils/format.ts,1,3,function,"function formatCurrency(amount: number, currency: string = 'USD'): string",1,3.950647 src/utils/validation.ts,8,12,function,"function validatePrice(price: number): ValidationResult",2,3.07557 src/index.ts,3,3,other,null,3,2.345138 totalCount: 10 help[2]: showing 3 of 10; refine the query with +term or -term,use extract with file/lineStart/lineEnd to retrieve a row's actual code content ``` Each row is one match: where it is (`file`, `lineStart`, `lineEnd`), what it is (`nodeKind`: function, class, interface, type alias and so on), its signature, and its `rank` and `finalScore`. Output uses [TOON](https://github.com/toon-format/spec), a table format that costs fewer tokens than JSON. ## Writing a query | You write | It means | | --- | --- | | `format price` | Code that mentions either word, ranked by how well it matches | | `"format price"` | The exact phrase | | `+cart` | Files must mention `cart` | | `-Button` | Skip files that mention `Button` | | `regex:use[A-Z]\w+` | Lines matching a regular expression | | `--exact` | Treat the whole query as one literal, operators and quotes included | Matching ignores case. A `-term` removes whole files, not single results. If one query mixes terms, `+cart -Button` finds code in files that mention `cart` but never `Button`: ``` $ monokl search "+cart -Button" . search[2]{file,lineStart,lineEnd,nodeKind,symbolSignature,rank,finalScore}: src/hooks/useCart.ts,11,25,function,function useCart(),1,1.453107 src/hooks/useCart.ts,5,9,interface,null,2,1.30166 ``` ## Options | Flag | Default | What it does | | --- | --- | --- | | `--max-results N` | 50 | Most results to print | | `--max-tokens N` | 20,000 | Most tokens of code to print | | `--max-bytes N` | 2 MiB | Most bytes of code to print | | `--tests` | off | Also search test files (`test/`, `tests/`, `__tests__/`, `spec/`, `*.test.*`, `*.spec.*`) | | `--no-ignore` | off | Also search hidden files and files that `.gitignore` or `.ignore` exclude | | `--language L` | all | Search one language only: `typescript`, `javascript` (`rust` and `python` are accepted but not supported yet) | ## Errors and exit codes - **0:** the search ran, even if nothing matched (you get `search: []`). - **1:** the search failed, for example an invalid regular expression or a directory that doesn't exist. The error is printed on stderr in the same compact format, with the cause. - **2:** the command line itself was wrong. ## Language support | Language | Status | | --- | --- | | TypeScript, JavaScript (`.ts`, `.tsx`, `.js`, `.jsx`, `.mjs`, `.cjs`, `.mts`, `.cts`; not `.d.ts`) | Search works today | | Rust | Designed, not built | | Python, Go, Java | Designed, not built | ## Why Existing code-search-for-agents tools are either fast but fuzzy (grep, embeddings) or precise but heavy (a full language server, a persistent daemon). monokl aims at the middle: real AST parsing without a language server, and no persistent index to keep warm. See [ARCHITECTURE.md](ARCHITECTURE.md) for how, and [PRINCIPLES.md](PRINCIPLES.md) for why. ## Docs | File | Covers | | --- | --- | | [ARCHITECTURE.md](ARCHITECTURE.md) | How it's built, in prose | | [PRINCIPLES.md](PRINCIPLES.md) | Design tenets and non-goals | | [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) | How to work on this repo | | [`docs/spec/`](docs/spec/README.md) | The full specification, including what's still to build | | [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) | Guidance for AI coding agents working in this repo | ## Name Monokl (MON-oh-kl) — from _monocle_, a single precision lens for close examination. The binary is `monokl`. ## License FSL-1.1-MIT — Functional Source License, converting to MIT two years after each release. See [`LICENSE`](LICENSE).

---
monokl: minor
---

First usable release. `monokl search` finds TypeScript and JavaScript code by structure and ranks it for AI coding agents.

- **Search returns whole code units.** Each result is the function, class, interface, type or export that matches, with its signature and line range, not a bare line.
- **Ranked, best first.** Functions, classes and methods rank above imports and re-exports, and names are split on `camelCase`, `snake_case` and acronyms, so `format price` finds `formatCurrency` and `validatePrice`.
- **A small query language.** Words, `"quoted phrases"`, `+required`, `-excluded` and `regex:` terms, plus `--exact` for a literal query.
- **Your project's rules apply.** `.gitignore`, `.ignore`, hidden, test and binary files are skipped by default, with `--tests` and `--no-ignore` to include them.
- **Sized for an agent's context.** Compact table output with paths relative to where you ran it, capped at 50 results, 20,000 tokens and 2 MiB (`--max-results`, `--max-tokens`, `--max-bytes`). When results are cut, the output says how many matched.
- **Predictable and robust.** The same search always returns the same output. An invalid pattern fails the whole search with a clear error. Files with syntax errors are still searched for what parsed, very deeply nested files are skipped safely, and an unreadable directory does not stop the search.

TypeScript and JavaScript only for now; the `extract`, `symbols`, `refs`, `definition` and `dependents` commands are not built yet.

Gets the first release going and documents what monokl does, by features rather than code.

## Why there was no release PR
Callisto only opens a release PR when a changeset is pending, and there wasn't one. The crate was also `publish = false`, so the release job reported "Nothing to release".

## What's in it
- **Publishing enabled.** `publish = false` is removed from the workspace and crate manifests. `cargo publish --dry-run` packages 43 files (119 KiB compressed) and builds clean.
- **A changeset (minor).** It describes the release as what a user can do. Once this merges, the Release workflow opens a PR that bumps `monokl` to 0.2.0 and writes the changelog; merging that PR publishes it.
- **README rewritten.** The old one said "spec-stage, no runnable binary" and promised commands that don't exist. The new one covers the features, the query language, every option and the exit codes, with real output from the `small-ts` fixtures. It says plainly what isn't built yet.

## Before you merge the release PR it opens
- Add the `CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN` repository secret.
- Allow GitHub Actions to create pull requests (Settings → Actions → General), or the workflow can't open the release PR.

## Two gaps found while documenting (not fixed here)
- The output ends with a hint to use an `extract` command, which doesn't exist yet.
- Diagnostics (unreadable files, a skipped language, "no positive terms", reaching the file ceiling) are computed but never printed, so those cases look like an empty result.

# Releasing

How a Callisto-managed release moves from changeset to published package.

For registry credential setup (npm, crates.io, PyPI), see [`publishing.md`](publishing.md).

---

## Local release: `callisto release`

`callisto release` selects packages without a tag for their current version. It publishes to registries, creates tags and GitHub releases, and records HEAD as the source. It can run on any branch.

- `callisto release --dry-run` prints the plan and performs no effect. It works anywhere, including on a dirty worktree or without an `origin` remote (tags are then noted as unbound).
- `--package <ecosystem/name>` (repeatable) restricts the run to named unreleased packages, plus every member of their fixed or linked groups. An unreleased workspace package that a selected one depends on (runtime, optional, or peer) must be selected too.
- It refuses a dirty worktree: a tracked modification or an untracked file not covered by `.gitignore`. Ignored files never count.
- It prints `Nothing to release.` and exits 0 when every package is already tagged.
- It prints a summary. With `--receipt <file>` it also writes the receipt there, only when every selected operation succeeded. An existing tag can exclude unfinished work before those operations are selected; see the retry limit below.
- A workspace with artifact slots or napi platform packages must release through CI. See the generated workflow below.

`cargo`, `npm`, `twine`, and `gh` report their own authentication failures. With the original release intent, the executor can adopt matching completed effects.

### Current retry limit

If a local release tags a version but fails before pushing the tag or completing GitHub work, a fresh `callisto release` can print `Nothing to release.` without a receipt.

- That message is not proof of completion.
- Generated simple workflows share this limit.
- CI releases based on the merged release PR retain the original package list.

---

## Generated workflows

`callisto init --workflow` (or answering yes to its prompt) writes `.github/workflows/callisto-release.yml`. Keep that filename for generated artifact releases.

Init never overwrites an existing file. This repo's [release workflow](../.github/workflows/callisto-release.yml) is a worked example.

- **Simple shape** (no artifact slots or napi platform packages): `version-pr` maintains the release PR. On each default-branch push, `release` runs `callisto release`; it is a no-op until an untagged version is merged.
- **Build-matrix shape** (artifact slots or napi platform packages): a release PR, then plan -> build -> publish. The build covers configured targets and artifact slots.
- Maturin builds, and platform packages without `napi.targets`, get no generated workflow.

Generated actions configure npm and Twine authentication during execution. Manual workflows must configure native authentication as described in [publishing.md](publishing.md).

Generated build support has these boundaries:

- Cargo `bin` targets can become GitHub release assets. npm `bin` and Python `[project.scripts]` are registry releases, not artifact products (E304).
- Co-located Cargo/Maturin manifests fail discovery with E007.
- Custom artifact builders need `--no-workflow` and a manual workflow that fills every configured artifact slot.
- Registry-only npm and PyPI releases need no artifact slots.

The default branch is the approval boundary: a merge to it publishes. Protect it with a rule that requires pull requests and reviews (GitHub -> Settings -> Rules). Init prints this reminder after writing the file.

Build-matrix limits:

- An addon crate outside the napi package directory needs a unique crate whose lib name matches `napi.binaryName` (E204).
- Generated `.node` files must be gitignored; release execution requires a clean checkout.
- Cargo `bin` targets build with `cargo build --release --locked`. Other products, such as `cdylib`s, need a manual workflow.
- The napi build/placement roster is currently workspace-wide, not narrowed to the release intent. Unrelated addons can block a release; this is tracked for correction, not a support requirement.
- Native npm lifecycle hooks run unchanged, including any owner-defined publishing or forge effects. Those effects are outside Callisto's release graph.

---

## Release PR and approval

The generated workflow keeps a release PR current. Merging that PR to the protected default branch authorizes publication; Callisto adds no approval step. Require reviews and CI checks in branch protection. A CODEOWNERS file alone does not enforce review.

The action's `version-pr` mode updates the PR; `release` runs `callisto release` for simple workspaces. Artifact and platform packages use plan/build/execute. See the [action inputs](../.github/actions/callisto-action/action.yml).

Only `execute` receives registry credentials. Keep `CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN`, `NPM_TOKEN`, and `TWINE_PASSWORD` out of workflow scope, planning and build jobs, and action inputs.

After a failed committed-decision CI release, "Re-run failed jobs" adopts completed effects and performs the rest. A green workflow alone is not proof of publication: check the receipt and providers.

## PR pre-flight verification

[`.github/actions/callisto-validate/action.yml`](../.github/actions/callisto-validate/action.yml) is a reusable action for your PR workflow:

- `callisto status --check` — one gate covering config health, package discovery, and changeset syntax: exit 0 with no error-level diagnostics, exit 1 otherwise.
- `callisto release --dry-run --format text` — simulates the release plan without effect.
- Writes a workspace status summary to the job's GitHub Actions summary page.

---

## Release identity and recovery

Every release run records two different revisions:

- The **orchestration revision**: the workflow and Callisto CLI that coordinate the run.
- The **release-source revision**: the merged release commit whose exact versions are released.

A recovery is a new run using current orchestration and an explicit full release-source SHA. It does not rerun historical workflow code, create a version PR, or invent a newer version.

To retry a failed run for the same source, use "Re-run failed jobs". Matching completed effects are adopted; conflicting or uncertain results stop the run. A receipt is written only after every selected operation succeeds.

## Recovering an older release

Recovering a commit that is no longer a branch tip may require these manual actions:

**E180: the workflow can't push tags.** GitHub rejects a `GITHUB_TOKEN` tag push when the tagged commit's workflows differ from every branch tip. Push every tag of the release yourself (PAT or deploy key), then dispatch the release for that SHA:

```sh
SHA=<release-source sha>
git tag -a "<tag>" -m "Release <tag>" "$SHA"   # each tag of the release
git push origin "<tag>"
gh workflow run callisto-release.yml --ref main -f release_source_sha="$SHA"
```

**`ArtifactAssetDiffers`: rebuilt assets don't match.** Rebuilt tarballs aren't byte-identical. Delete the mismatched assets and dispatch again:

```sh
gh release delete-asset "<release tag>" "<asset>" --yes   # each mismatched asset
gh workflow run callisto-release.yml --ref main -f release_source_sha="$SHA"
```

## Publication checks

Callisto checks the registry, remote tag, and GitHub release before each effect. An exact match is adopted; a conflict or uncertain result stops the run. Check the receipt and providers before treating a release as complete.

Registry checks confirm version presence, not identical bytes, the npm dist-tag, or a complete Python wheel/sdist set. A partial PyPI upload can therefore be mistaken for a complete version. See [publishing limits](publishing.md#current-python-support-limits).

GitHub Releases start as drafts. Assets upload before the release is made public.

---

## Platform-package publish order

`callisto release execute` follows the derived operation DAG, not a fixed global Cargo -> npm -> PyPI pipeline. Native dependency edges and attached npm platform prerequisites constrain that order. Platform packages publish before their npm owner.

A napi-rs distribution can publish N platform-specific npm packages plus one owner package whose `optionalDependencies` pin their versions. Maturin instead produces Python wheels and optionally an sdist under one PyPI distribution/version; those are files, not npm platform packages.

- **A platform package fails**: its owner's main package is never attempted, so no `optionalDependencies` point at a version that was never uploaded. Fix the cause and re-run — it adopts every effect that already landed.
- **A platform dependency is missing from the selection entirely**: planning refuses (`ReleaseSelectionInvalid`, "select it too") before anything is published.

For a package with both Cargo and npm distributions, one registry publish can still lag behind its shared tag or public GitHub release. Do not treat that announcement as proof that both distributions are available.

input.command: cat /Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/.github/workflows/callisto-release.yml
input.description: Read callisto build-matrix release workflow

result.output:
name: Release

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      release_source_sha:
        description: 'Merged managed release-PR commit to recover; leave empty for the triggering commit.'
        required: false
        type: string

permissions: {}

# One group per commit: GitHub replaces a pending run in a shared group, which
# could silently drop a release merge queued behind an unrelated push.
concurrency:
  group: release-${{ github.sha }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  verify:
    name: Verify release candidate
    if: github.event_name == 'push' || inputs.release_source_sha == ''
    timeout-minutes: 45
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Build local Callisto
        uses: $/.github/actions/setup-callisto
        with:
          source: local

      - name: Install just
        uses: taiki-e/install-action@7623a79cdfecb99d681017af368ca353d9f49bb5 # v2
        with:
          tool: just@1.58.0

      - name: Format Check
        run: just fmt-check

      - name: Clippy Lints
        run: just lint

      - name: Install release verification tools
        uses: taiki-e/install-action@7623a79cdfecb99d681017af368ca353d9f49bb5 # v2
        with:
          tool: cargo-nextest,ripgrep

      - name: Unit & Integration Tests
        run: just test

      - name: Install cargo-deny
        uses: taiki-e/install-action@7623a79cdfecb99d681017af368ca353d9f49bb5 # v2
        with:
          tool: cargo-deny

      - name: Supply Chain Audit
        run: just audit

      - name: Verify workflow contracts and reject mutable action references
        run: just workflow-contracts

  recovery-checks:
    name: Check release workflow policy for recovery
    if: github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && inputs.release_source_sha != ''
    timeout-minutes: 10
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - name: Install ripgrep
        uses: taiki-e/install-action@7623a79cdfecb99d681017af368ca353d9f49bb5 # v2
        with:
          tool: ripgrep
      - name: Install just
        uses: taiki-e/install-action@7623a79cdfecb99d681017af368ca353d9f49bb5 # v2
        with:
          tool: just@1.58.0
      - name: Verify release workflow contracts
        run: just release-workflow-checks

  release-candidate:
    name: Identify a merged Callisto release PR
    needs: [verify, recovery-checks]
    # Exactly one gate runs per event; a failed gate matches neither clause.
    if: >-
      always() && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' &&
      ((needs.verify.result == 'success' && needs.recovery-checks.result == 'skipped') ||
       (needs.recovery-checks.result == 'success' && needs.verify.result == 'skipped'))
    timeout-minutes: 10
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
      pull-requests: read
    outputs:
      is_release_pr: ${{ steps.candidate.outputs.is_release_pr }}
      release_source_sha: ${{ steps.candidate.outputs.release_source_sha }}
      orchestration_sha: ${{ steps.candidate.outputs.orchestration_sha }}
    steps:
      - id: candidate
        shell: bash
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          RELEASE_SOURCE_SHA_INPUT: ${{ inputs.release_source_sha }}
          TRIGGERING_SHA: ${{ github.sha }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          release_source_sha="${RELEASE_SOURCE_SHA_INPUT:-$TRIGGERING_SHA}"
          if [[ ! "$release_source_sha" =~ ^[0-9a-f]{40}$ ]]; then
            echo "::error::release_source_sha must be exactly 40 lowercase hex characters"
            exit 1
          fi
          resolved_sha=$(gh api "/repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/commits/${release_source_sha}" --jq '.sha')
          if [[ "$resolved_sha" != "$release_source_sha" ]]; then
            echo "::error::release_source_sha does not resolve to that exact commit"
            exit 1
          fi
          # Attestations are stamped with this run's own SHA, so the
          # coordinator must be exactly the revision running this workflow.
          orchestration_sha="$TRIGGERING_SHA"
          # This only schedules the job. `release plan` verifies the actual
          # parent-to-merge delta; labels and PR metadata are never authority.
          # The GitHub API check is complementary provenance evidence: a
          # trusted merge must be both an actual merge of the managed PR and
          # a GitHub-verified signed commit. It cannot be a direct push.
          prs=$(gh api --paginate "/repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/commits/${release_source_sha}/pulls" --jq '[.[] | select(.merged_at != null and .base.ref == "main" and .head.repo.full_name == "'"${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}"'" and (.head.ref == "callisto/version-packages" or (.head.ref | test("^callisto/version-packages--[0-9a-f]{40}$"))))] | length')
          verified=$(gh api "/repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/commits/${release_source_sha}" --jq '.commit.verification.verified')
          if [[ "$prs" == 1 && "$verified" == true ]]; then
            {
              echo 'is_release_pr=true'
              echo "release_source_sha=$release_source_sha"
              echo "orchestration_sha=$orchestration_sha"
            } >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          else
            echo 'is_release_pr=false' >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

  version-pr:
    name: Create or update the Callisto release PR
    needs: release-candidate
    if: >-
      always() && needs.release-candidate.result == 'success' &&
      needs.release-candidate.outputs.is_release_pr != 'true' &&
      inputs.release_source_sha == ''
    timeout-minutes: 10
    concurrency:
      group: version-pr
      cancel-in-progress: false
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: write
      pull-requests: write
    outputs:
      has_pending_changesets: ${{ steps.version-pr.outputs.hasChangesets }}

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: $/.github/actions/setup-callisto
        with:
          source: local
      - name: Compose, version, and open the release PR
        id: version-pr
        uses: $/.github/actions/callisto-action
        with:
          setup_callisto: 'false'
          branch: main
          release_branch: callisto/version-packages
          # Interdependent Cargo packages bump together, so Cargo.lock must be refreshed in the release PR.
          version_command: 'callisto version --refresh-lockfiles'
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}

  plan:
    name: Derive ephemeral intent from the merged release commit
    needs: release-candidate
    # always(): release-candidate's own ancestors include a gate that is skipped
    # by design, and a skipped ancestor silently skips any job without a status function.
    if: >-
      always() && needs.release-candidate.result == 'success' &&
      needs.release-candidate.outputs.is_release_pr == 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 20
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
    outputs:
      has_artifacts: ${{ steps.slots.outputs.has_artifacts }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          # The coordinator must be the current workflow revision. Recovery
          # never rebuilds its release engine from historic source.
          ref: ${{ needs.release-candidate.outputs.orchestration_sha }}
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: $/.github/actions/setup-callisto
        with:
          source: local
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          ref: ${{ needs.release-candidate.outputs.release_source_sha }}
          path: release-source
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false
      - name: Derive and hash intent
        env:
          RELEASE_SOURCE_SHA: ${{ needs.release-candidate.outputs.release_source_sha }}
          ORCHESTRATION_SHA: ${{ needs.release-candidate.outputs.orchestration_sha }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          handoff_dir="${RUNNER_TEMP}/release-intent"
          mkdir -p "$handoff_dir"
          callisto release plan --source-root "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/release-source" \
            --orchestration-revision "$ORCHESTRATION_SHA" --artifact-repository "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" \
            --from-release-commit "$RELEASE_SOURCE_SHA" \
            --decision "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/release-source/.callisto/release-decision.json" \
            --out "$handoff_dir/release-intent.json"
          # Relative name: the consumers verify from a different runner OS and RUNNER_TEMP.
          (cd "$handoff_dir" && shasum -a 256 release-intent.json > release-intent.json.sha256)
      - name: Read declared artifact slot count
        id: slots
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # Own statement: set -e cannot see a substitution failing inside an echo argument.
          has_artifacts=$(jq '.artifactSlots | length > 0' "${RUNNER_TEMP}/release-intent/release-intent.json")
          case "$has_artifacts" in
            true|false) ;;
            *) echo "::error::artifact slot probe returned '$has_artifacts'"; exit 1 ;;
          esac
          echo "has_artifacts=$has_artifacts" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: release-intent
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/release-intent
          if-no-files-found: error
          # 1 day was too short: a stuck run needing "execute" re-run days
          # later (e.g. while a workflow bug gets diagnosed and fixed) loses
          # this artifact before the fix even lands, forcing a full rerun
          # instead of just the failed job.
          retention-days: 7

  build-artifact:
    name: Build ${{ matrix.target }} from the intent-bound source tree
    needs: [plan, release-candidate]
    if: always() && needs.plan.result == 'success' && needs.plan.outputs.has_artifacts == 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 45
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - id: macos-arm64
            runner: macos-14
            target: aarch64-apple-darwin
            asset: callisto-aarch64-apple-darwin.tar.gz
            kind: cli
          - id: linux-gnu
            runner: ubuntu-latest
            target: x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu
            asset: callisto-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.gz
            kind: cli
          - id: linux-musl
            runner: ubuntu-latest
            target: x86_64-unknown-linux-musl
            asset: callisto-x86_64-unknown-linux-musl.tar.gz
            kind: cross
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.runner }}
    permissions:
      contents: read
      attestations: write
      id-token: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          ref: ${{ needs.release-candidate.outputs.orchestration_sha }}
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: $/.github/actions/setup-callisto
        with:
          source: local
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          ref: ${{ needs.release-candidate.outputs.release_source_sha }}
          path: release-source
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8.0.1
        with:
          name: release-intent
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/release-intent
      - name: Verify handoff
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          handoff_dir="${RUNNER_TEMP}/release-intent"
          (cd "$handoff_dir" && shasum -a 256 -c release-intent.json.sha256)
          callisto release inspect --input "$handoff_dir/release-intent.json"
          mkdir -p "${RUNNER_TEMP}/release-artifacts"
      - name: Build declared artifact
        env:
          CALLISTO_RELEASE_ARTIFACT_KIND: ${{ matrix.kind }}
          CALLISTO_RELEASE_ARTIFACT_TARGET: ${{ matrix.target }}
          CALLISTO_RELEASE_ARTIFACT_ASSET: ${{ matrix.asset }}
          CALLISTO_RELEASE_SOURCE_ROOT: ${{ github.workspace }}/release-source
          CALLISTO_RELEASE_ARTIFACT_DIR: ${{ runner.temp }}/release-artifacts
        run: |
          bash .github/scripts/build-release-artifact.sh
      - name: Attest exact artifact bytes
        uses: actions/attest-build-provenance@4d101475d8b20a2381f78447822ac1eab6504dd8 # v4.2.2
        with:
          subject-path: ${{ runner.temp }}/release-artifacts/${{ matrix.asset }}
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: release-build-${{ matrix.id }}
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/release-artifacts/${{ matrix.asset }}
          if-no-files-found: error
          # 1 day was too short: a stuck run needing "execute" re-run days
          # later (e.g. while a workflow bug gets diagnosed and fixed) loses
          # this artifact before the fix even lands, forcing a full rerun
          # instead of just the failed job.
          retention-days: 7

  build:
    name: Assemble attested product artifacts
    needs: [build-artifact, release-candidate, plan]
    if: always() && needs.plan.outputs.has_artifacts == 'true' && needs.build-artifact.result == 'success'
    timeout-minutes: 15
    outputs:
      orchestration_sha: ${{ needs.release-candidate.outputs.orchestration_sha }}
      release_source_sha: ${{ needs.release-candidate.outputs.release_source_sha }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          ref: ${{ needs.release-candidate.outputs.orchestration_sha }}
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: $/.github/actions/setup-callisto
        with:
          source: local
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8.0.1
        with:
          name: release-intent
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/release-intent
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8.0.1
        with:
          name: release-build-macos-arm64
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/release-artifacts
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8.0.1
        with:
          name: release-build-linux-gnu
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/release-artifacts
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8.0.1
        with:
          name: release-build-linux-musl
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/release-artifacts
      - name: Create exact artifact manifest
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          callisto release artifact-manifest --intent "${RUNNER_TEMP}/release-intent/release-intent.json" --artifact-dir "${RUNNER_TEMP}/release-artifacts" --out "${RUNNER_TEMP}/release-artifacts/manifest.json"
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: release-build
          path: |
            ${{ runner.temp }}/release-intent
            ${{ runner.temp }}/release-artifacts
          if-no-files-found: error
          retention-days: 7

  execute:
    name: Execute approved release
    needs: [plan, build, release-candidate]
    # Artifact-less sources skip build; a failed or cancelled build must still block.
    # !cancelled() not always(): a status function still defeats the skipped-ancestor
    # rule, but cancelling the run must stop the one irreversible job.
    if: >-
      !cancelled() && needs.plan.result == 'success' &&
      (needs.plan.outputs.has_artifacts == 'false' || needs.build.result == 'success')
    timeout-minutes: 60
    concurrency:
      group: release-execute
      cancel-in-progress: false
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: write
      attestations: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          ref: ${{ needs.release-candidate.outputs.orchestration_sha }}
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: $/.github/actions/setup-callisto
        with:
          source: local
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          ref: ${{ needs.release-candidate.outputs.release_source_sha }}
          path: release-source
          fetch-depth: 0
          # The release-source checkout alone needs Git credentials because
          # graph-owned tag dispatch pushes from this repository.
          persist-credentials: true
      # Downloaded outside the workspace (under $RUNNER_TEMP, like
      # setup-callisto's own binary install): callisto release execute
      # re-checks release trust before every dispatch, which requires a
      # worktree with no tracked or untracked files -- landing these inside
      # the checkout would dirty it and fail that check before anything
      # gets published.
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8.0.1
        with:
          name: release-intent
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/release-intent
      - if: needs.plan.outputs.has_artifacts == 'true'
        uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8.0.1
        with:
          name: release-build
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/release-build
      - name: Verify same-run handoff before credentials
        env:
          HAS_ARTIFACTS: ${{ needs.plan.outputs.has_artifacts }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          intent_dir="${RUNNER_TEMP}/release-intent"
          build_dir="${RUNNER_TEMP}/release-build"
          (cd "$intent_dir" && shasum -a 256 -c release-intent.json.sha256)
          if [[ "$HAS_ARTIFACTS" == true ]]; then
            cmp "$intent_dir/release-intent.json" "$build_dir/release-intent/release-intent.json"
          fi
      - name: Execute verified release
        env:
          CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN }}
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          ORCHESTRATION_SHA: ${{ needs.release-candidate.outputs.orchestration_sha }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          intent_dir="${RUNNER_TEMP}/release-intent"
          build_dir="${RUNNER_TEMP}/release-build"
          receipt_dir="${RUNNER_TEMP}/callisto-release-receipt/${GITHUB_RUN_ID}"
          mkdir -p "$receipt_dir"
          args=(--source-root "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/release-source" --intent "$intent_dir/release-intent.json" --receipt "$receipt_dir/release-receipt.json" --orchestration-revision "$ORCHESTRATION_SHA")
          if [[ -f "$build_dir/release-artifacts/manifest.json" ]]; then
            args+=(--artifact-manifest "$build_dir/release-artifacts/manifest.json" --artifact-dir "$build_dir/release-artifacts")
          fi
          callisto release execute "${args[@]}"
      - name: Summarize receipt
        if: always()
        run: |
          receipt="${RUNNER_TEMP}/callisto-release-receipt/${GITHUB_RUN_ID}/release-receipt.json"
          if [[ -f "$receipt" ]]; then
            {
              echo '### Release receipt'
              echo '```json'
              cat "$receipt"
              echo '```'
            } >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          fi
      - name: Upload receipt
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          # Per attempt: keeps each attempt's receipt instead of shadowing the prior one.
          name: release-receipt-attempt-${{ github.run_attempt }}
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/callisto-release-receipt/${{ github.run_id }}
          if-no-files-found: ignore
          retention-days: 7

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Build one declared Callisto product artifact. This script deliberately owns
# only platform compilation and archive layout; Callisto owns all release
# planning, artifact identity, provenance verification, and publication.
set -euo pipefail

: "${CALLISTO_RELEASE_ARTIFACT_KIND:?must name cli or cross}"
: "${CALLISTO_RELEASE_ARTIFACT_TARGET:?must name a supported Rust target}"
: "${CALLISTO_RELEASE_ARTIFACT_ASSET:?must name the expected release asset}"
: "${CALLISTO_RELEASE_SOURCE_ROOT:?must name the checked-out source root}"
: "${CALLISTO_RELEASE_ARTIFACT_DIR:?must name an output directory}"

kind="$CALLISTO_RELEASE_ARTIFACT_KIND"
target="$CALLISTO_RELEASE_ARTIFACT_TARGET"
asset="$CALLISTO_RELEASE_ARTIFACT_ASSET"
source_root="$CALLISTO_RELEASE_SOURCE_ROOT"
artifact_dir="$CALLISTO_RELEASE_ARTIFACT_DIR"

case "$kind:$target:$asset" in

Nothing is done yet: I'm blocked on git, and I made one mistake along the way.

**The block:** the sandbox guard refuses every `git` call here (`fetch`, `status`, `git -C …`), saying it can't verify they stay inside this worktree. Without git I can't branch off the merged `main`, commit, or push.

**The mistake:** I tried to run `callisto init` in a scratch copy. Creating the scratch directory failed, and my command carried on in the real worktree. It deleted `callisto.toml` and `.github/workflows/callisto-release.yml`. I rewrote both from what I'd read earlier. `callisto status --check` still works, but I can't run `git diff` to prove the files are byte-identical. Please run `! git diff --stat` in the worktree. It should show no changes to those two files.

**What callisto and caliper do for binaries** (read from the local repos):
- **Config:** `callisto.toml` has `[release] product-package` and `forge-repository`, one `[[release.artifact]]` per target, and `publish-to = ["crates-io", "github-release"]` on the CLI package.
- **Workflow:** `callisto init --workflow --artifact-target …` generates the build-matrix `callisto-release.yml`. It runs release PR → plan → per-target build → attested artifacts → execute, with a small `.github/scripts/build-release-artifact.sh` per repo.
- **Targets:** callisto uses `aarch64-apple-darwin`, `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu` and `x86_64-unknown-linux-musl` (musl via `cross`). The Homebrew formula also lists Intel mac and arm64 Linux.
- **Distribution:** assets are tagged `<pkg>@<version>`. There's a `proto/<tool>.toml` plugin and a formula in `/Users/gabe/Projects/homebrew-tap`, updated by `tools/update_formula.py`.

**One more blocker:** `origin` still points at `github.com/orin-axi/monokl.git`, and `callisto init` fails with E187 because it must match `orin-dx/monokl`. I can fix it with `git remote set-url origin https://github.com/orin-dx/monokl.git` once git works.

1. Branch `feat/release-binaries` from `main`.
2. Run `callisto init` with four targets: `aarch64-apple-darwin`, `x86_64-apple-darwin`, `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu` and `x86_64-unknown-linux-musl`.
3. Copy the build script and the proto plugin, and add the Homebrew formula to the tap.
4. Add a changeset.
5. Update the README install section and fix the stale "not on crates.io" line.
6. Open a PR.
7. Fix the diagnostics and `extract` hint gaps in a separate PR.

name: Update formula

on:
  repository_dispatch:
    types: [tool_released]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      tool:
        description: Formula to update
        required: true
        type: string
      tag:
        description: Published release tag; leave empty to check the latest stable release
        required: false
        type: string
  schedule:
    - cron: '17 8 * * *'

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  select:
    if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && github.repository == 'orin-dx/homebrew-tap'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    outputs:
      tools: ${{ steps.select.outputs.tools }}
      tag: ${{ steps.select.outputs.tag }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - id: select
        env:
          EVENT: ${{ github.event_name }}
          INPUT_TOOL: ${{ inputs.tool }}
          INPUT_TAG: ${{ inputs.tag }}
          RELEASE_TOOL: ${{ github.event.client_payload.tool }}
          RELEASE_TAG: ${{ github.event.client_payload.tag }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          case "$EVENT" in
            schedule)
              tools=$(python3 scripts/update_formula.py --list-tools)
              echo "tools=$tools" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
              echo 'tag=' >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
              ;;
            workflow_dispatch)
              python3 scripts/update_formula.py --validate-tool "$INPUT_TOOL"
              if [[ -n "$INPUT_TAG" && ! "$INPUT_TAG" =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._@/+\-]{0,127}$ ]]; then
                echo 'Invalid release tag' >&2
                exit 1
              fi
              echo "tools=[\"${INPUT_TOOL}\"]" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
              echo "tag=${INPUT_TAG}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
              ;;
            repository_dispatch)
              python3 scripts/update_formula.py --validate-tool "$RELEASE_TOOL"
              if [[ ! "$RELEASE_TAG" =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._@/+\-]{0,127}$ ]]; then
                echo 'Invalid release tag' >&2
                exit 1
              fi
              echo "tools=[\"${RELEASE_TOOL}\"]" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
              echo "tag=${RELEASE_TAG}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
              ;;
            *) exit 1 ;;
          esac

  update:
    needs: select
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        tool: ${{ fromJSON(needs.select.outputs.tools) }}
    concurrency:
      group: formula-${{ matrix.tool }}
      cancel-in-progress: false
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 20
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - name: Verify release and update formula
        id: formula
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          TOOL: ${{ matrix.tool }}
          RELEASE_TAG: ${{ needs.select.outputs.tag }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          if [[ -n "$RELEASE_TAG" ]]; then
            version=$(python3 scripts/update_formula.py --tool "$TOOL" --tag "$RELEASE_TAG")
          else
            version=$(python3 scripts/update_formula.py --tool "$TOOL" --latest)
          fi
          echo "version=$version" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          if git diff --quiet -- "Formula/${TOOL}.rb"; then
            echo 'changed=false' >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          else
            echo 'changed=true' >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi
      - name: Create tap-scoped GitHub App token
        if: steps.formula.outputs.changed == 'true'
        id: app-token
        uses: actions/create-github-app-token@64ab729a6294000f5aa4a4bc0b73d1f32bc45510 # v3
        with:
          client-id: ${{ vars.TAP_APP_CLIENT_ID }}
          private-key: ${{ secrets.TAP_APP_PRIVATE_KEY }}
          owner: orin-dx
          repositories: homebrew-tap
          permission-contents: write
          permission-pull-requests: write
      - name: Open update pull request
        if: steps.formula.outputs.changed == 'true'
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token }}
          TOOL: ${{ matrix.tool }}
          RELEASE_VERSION: ${{ steps.formula.outputs.version }}
          APP_SLUG: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.app-slug }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          branch="automation/${TOOL}-${RELEASE_VERSION}"
          if [[ "$(gh pr list --repo orin-dx/homebrew-tap --head "$branch" --state open --json number --jq 'length')" != 0 ]]; then
            echo "An update pull request is already open for $TOOL $RELEASE_VERSION"
            exit 0
          fi
          if git ls-remote --exit-code --heads origin "$branch" > /dev/null; then
            echo "An update branch already exists for $TOOL $RELEASE_VERSION; inspect it before retrying." >&2
            exit 1
          fi
          bot_id=$(gh api "users/${APP_SLUG}[bot]" --jq .id)
          git config user.name "${APP_SLUG}[bot]"
          git config user.email "${bot_id}+${APP_SLUG}[bot]@users.noreply.github.com"

# How tap updates work

The tap follows published CLI releases. It does not decide when Callisto or Caliper publishes, and a release workflow does not write a formula directly.

## The path from release to PR

1. A trusted release workflow sends `tool_released` with a tool name and tag. The tap also checks for new stable versions every day, so a missed event does not strand a release.
2. [`scripts/update_formula.py`](../scripts/update_formula.py) reads the tool's committed manifest. It fetches publisher metadata and every platform archive, verifies the published digest, checks archive contents and executable mode, then writes four SHA-256 values to the formula.
3. The tap creates a short-lived GitHub App token scoped to this repository and opens a branch and PR. It does not overwrite an existing update branch or downgrade a formula.
4. **Required tap checks** runs updater tests, then audits, installs, and exercises the changed formula on macOS ARM/Intel and Linux ARM/x86-64. Shared updater changes and a weekly run check every formula. A maintainer reviews and approves the PR, including any new runtime library or minimum OS requirements.

The event cannot choose a download URL or checksum. Both come from the manifest on `main` and the publisher's versioned release. The SHA-256 in a merged formula is the digest Homebrew checks on every later install.

## One-time GitHub setup

### Create the App

Create an organization-owned GitHub App called something like `orin-dx-homebrew-updater`. Disable its webhook. Give it only **Contents: read and write** and **Pull requests: read and write**, then install it on **only `orin-dx/homebrew-tap`**. The notification needs Contents write for GitHub's `repository_dispatch` endpoint; the tap also needs Pull requests write to open the review PR.

Generate one private key and record the App's client ID. Keep the PEM out of Git and terminal output. Store them as an organization Actions variable and secret, each visible only to `homebrew-tap`, `callisto`, and `caliper`:

```sh
gh variable set TAP_APP_CLIENT_ID --org orin-dx --repos homebrew-tap,callisto,caliper
gh secret set TAP_APP_PRIVATE_KEY --org orin-dx --repos homebrew-tap,callisto,caliper < path/to/downloaded-key.pem
```

The variable command prompts for the client ID. The secret command reads the PEM from stdin; delete the downloaded file after storing it. Add Firkin to the selected repositories only when its release notifier exists. The App never needs access to the source repositories themselves.

### Protect `main`

After the first tap commit lands, add a repository ruleset for `main`: require a PR, one approval, dismiss stale approvals after new pushes, and require **Required tap checks**. Do not give the App a bypass. The sole maintainer can use an admin PR-only bypass for human-authored maintenance; bot formula PRs still need that maintainer's approval. Leave automatic merge off.

The tap workflow's default `GITHUB_TOKEN` is read-only. Its App token is minted only after all archives pass verification and only for `homebrew-tap`. Source repositories use the same shared [notification action](https://github.com/orin-dx/actions/tree/main/notify-homebrew-tap) after a successful release, with their receipt proving a CLI was published. They have no formula-editing code.

## Run or recover an update

Run **Update formula** in the tap's Actions tab or use the CLI:

```sh
gh workflow run update-formula.yml -R orin-dx/homebrew-tap -f tool=caliper
gh workflow run update-formula.yml -R orin-dx/homebrew-tap -f tool=callisto -f tag=callisto@0.14.2
```

Without App credentials, verification still runs but the workflow cannot open a changed-formula PR. You can run the updater locally and submit a human PR instead. If an update branch already exists, inspect its PR and branch before retrying; the workflow refuses to force-push over it. To rotate the App key, replace `TAP_APP_PRIVATE_KEY` in the selected organization secret and revoke the old key in the App's settings.

See [Contributing](../CONTRIBUTING.md) for formula changes and [Security](../SECURITY.md) for private reporting.
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Choose formula checks for a change while keeping shared changes comprehensive."""

import argparse
import json
import re
import subprocess
from typing import Optional
from update_formula import ROOT, list_tools

SHARED_PATHS = {".github/workflows/ci.yml", ".github/workflows/update-formula.yml"}
TOOL_PATH = re.compile(r"^(?:Formula/([a-z][a-z0-9-]*)\.rb|tools/([a-z][a-z0-9-]*)\.json)$")


def select_tools(paths: list[str], available: list[str]) -> list[str]:
    if any(path.startswith("scripts/") or path in SHARED_PATHS for path in paths):
        return available
    changed = {match.group(1) or match.group(2) for path in paths if (match := TOOL_PATH.fullmatch(path))}
    missing = changed.difference(available)
    if missing:
        raise ValueError(f"Changed formula has no tool manifest: {', '.join(sorted(missing))}")
    return sorted(changed)


def changed_paths(base: str) -> Optional[list[str]]:
    if not base or set(base) == {"0"}:
        return None
    result = subprocess.run(
        ["git", "diff", "--no-renames", "--name-only", base, "HEAD", "--"],
        cwd=ROOT,
        check=True,
        capture_output=True,
        text=True,
    )
    return result.stdout.splitlines()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("--base", default="")
    parser.add_argument("--all", action="store_true", help="Check every formula, for a periodic full run")
    args = parser.parse_args()
    available = list_tools(ROOT)
    paths = None if args.all else changed_paths(args.base)
    print(json.dumps(available if paths is None else select_tools(paths, available)))

Here's the integration plan, based on the tap's contributing guide and updater.

**What the tap requires**
- **Targets:** exactly four, `macos-arm64`, `macos-x64`, `linux-arm64` and `linux-x64`. The Linux builds must be GNU/glibc. A musl build can't be the tap archive.
- **Archive:** each target needs a `.tar.gz` GitHub release asset whose only required member is the `monokl` binary. The asset needs a GitHub-published `sha256:` digest, and the release must be published and stable (not a draft or prerelease).
- **Tag:** `monokl@<version>`, which callisto already produces.
- **Formula:** a `test do` block running a real workflow, the license, and one URL plus SHA-256 per platform.
- **Tap files:** `Formula/monokl.rb`, `tools/monokl.json`, a row in the README tool list, and `docs/tools/monokl.md`.
- **Notification:** `tool_released` from monokl's release workflow via `orin-dx/actions/notify-homebrew-tap`. The daily cron also catches missed releases.

**Plan, in order**
1. **monokl PR (binaries).** `callisto.toml` gets `[release]` and `forge-repository = "orin-dx/monokl"`, four `[[release.artifact]]` entries, and `publish-to = ["crates-io", "github-release"]`. The generated build-matrix workflow replaces the simple one. The build script covers `aarch64-apple-darwin`, `x86_64-apple-darwin`, `aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu` and `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu`. Callisto's own script doesn't build the two missing targets, so I'll add them. The Linux ARM build probably needs `cross` or an arm runner. I'd skip musl, since the tap doesn't use it and a proto plugin could do without it.
2. **Notify step.** After a successful release, call the notify action with `tool: monokl`. This needs `TAP_APP_CLIENT_ID` and `TAP_APP_PRIVATE_KEY` shared with monokl, which is an org-level variable and secret, so only you can do that:

content.text:
Yes, this is what the tap expects. I checked the setup doc against the workflow code that consumes it.

**What the code reads** (`update-formula.yml` lines 105–109, and the notify action):
- `vars.TAP_APP_CLIENT_ID` is an Actions **variable**, not a secret.
- `secrets.TAP_APP_PRIVATE_KEY` is the PEM contents.
- The token is minted for `owner: orin-dx`, `repositories: homebrew-tap`, with `permission-contents: write` and `permission-pull-requests: write`. The notify action asks for contents write only.
- So the App needs exactly **Contents: read & write** and **Pull requests: read & write**, installed on `homebrew-tap` alone.

**The value to copy is the Client ID, not the App ID.** The action's input is `client-id`. On the App's settings page it looks like `Iv23…`. The numeric "App ID" shown beside it is not what this workflow takes.

**Creating it:**
1. Go to github.com/organizations/orin-dx/settings/apps → **New GitHub App**.
2. Set the name (e.g. `orin-dx-homebrew-updater`) and the homepage URL (e.g. `https://orin-dx.com`).
3. Untick **Webhook → Active**.
4. Under **Repository permissions**, set **Contents** to Read and write and **Pull requests** to Read and write. Metadata: Read is added automatically. Leave everything else at No access.
5. Set "Where can this GitHub App be installed?" to **Only on this account**, then click **Create**.
6. On the App page, copy the **Client ID**, then click **Generate a private key**. A `.pem` downloads.
7. Open **Install App** → orin-dx → **Only select repositories** → `homebrew-tap` only.
8. Store the values, from a terminal where `gh` has org admin rights:
   ```sh
   gh variable set TAP_APP_CLIENT_ID --org orin-dx --visibility selected --repos homebrew-tap,callisto,caliper,monokl
   gh secret set TAP_APP_PRIVATE_KEY --org orin-dx --visibility selected --repos homebrew-tap,callisto,caliper,monokl < ~/Downloads/<key>.pem
   ```
   Delete the `.pem` afterwards.
9. After the first tap commit, add the `main` ruleset the doc describes: PR required, one approval, stale approvals dismissed, **Required tap checks** required, and no App bypass.

**Two things I couldn't confirm:**
- **No sibling repo notifies the tap yet.** I searched the local `callisto` and `caliper` checkouts and found no call to the notify action. Either those checkouts are behind their remotes, or the notify step isn't wired in. Until I check each repo's remote `main`, I can't say whether monokl should copy an existing step or add the first one. I won't need the App for the binaries PR, so this doesn't block it.
- **Whether the App already exists.** My install lookup timed out. If you find one under Developer settings, reuse it and skip steps 1–7, but check its permissions against the list above.
[Image #1] What do I set here?
[Image: source: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-gabe-Projects-monokl--claude-worktrees-first-release/5bd0620b-ff9a-4f78-8d5f-5208ce4257e8/images/1.png]

Leave nearly everything on this part of the form as it is. Only the permissions need changing.

**Leave alone** (the App never authorizes users, so none of the identity settings apply):
- **Redirect URI:** empty. Click **Delete** on the blank row if the form won't submit with it. The field isn't required.
- **Allow wildcard matching, Request user authorization (OAuth), Enable Device Flow:** unchecked.
- **Expire user authorization tokens:** leave the default (checked). It has no effect here.
- **Setup URL, Redirect on update:** empty and unchecked.
- **Webhook Active:** unchecked, as you have it. Leave URL and Secret empty.
- **Where can this GitHub App be installed?:** keep **Only on this account**.

**Set these** under Permissions. Expand **Repository permissions**:
- **Contents:** Read and write.
- **Pull requests:** Read and write.
- **Metadata:** shows Read-only automatically. Leave it.

Leave **Organization**, **Account** and **Enterprise** permissions untouched. The "user permissions" line above them is just a page label.

Then click **Create GitHub App**. On the next page, copy the **Client ID** and use **Generate a private key**. Install it on `homebrew-tap` only, as in steps 6 and 7 of my earlier list.
Are you sure that is enough?

Yes, for the App itself. I traced every call that uses its token, and each is covered by Contents and Pull requests (both read and write).

| Call | Where | Permission |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `repository_dispatch` (`tool_released`) | notify action | Contents: write |
| `git push` of the `automation/<tool>-<version>` branch | `update-formula.yml` | Contents: write |
| `gh pr list` and `gh pr create` | `update-formula.yml` | Pull requests: read/write |
| `gh api users/<slug>[bot]` | `update-formula.yml` | none (public) |
| Metadata | every call | read, granted automatically |

The push only touches `Formula/<tool>.rb`, so the **Workflows** permission isn't needed. It would be if a bot commit edited anything under `.github/workflows`.

The App can't work until you also do these outside the form:
1. **Install it on `homebrew-tap`.** Creating the App doesn't install it. The token action fails with a 404 until it's installed there.
2. **Set the variable and secret with `monokl` in the repo list.** The release job can only read org values for repos on the selected list.
3. **Don't give the App a bypass on the `main` ruleset.** It should only push `automation/*` branches and open PRs. The doc requires a human approval on every bot PR.
4. **Release PRs need no extra setup for this.** Because an App token opened the PR, CI runs on it (a `GITHUB_TOKEN` PR wouldn't trigger it).

One thing I haven't verified: the exact name of the required check. The doc says **Required tap checks**, but `ci.yml` is named "Formula checks" and I only read its first 60 lines. When you set up the ruleset, pick the check from the dropdown after one CI run rather than typing the name.

The `main` ruleset and required approvals limit the damage, but a leaked key is still a way to put arbitrary branches and PRs in the tap.

The tap workflow is the only place that needs the key to open PRs. The source repos use it only to send the release notification, and the tap's daily cron picks up releases without it.   # Separate from `execute` so the tap App key never shares a job with the registry token.
  notify-tap:
    needs: execute
    if: needs.execute.result == 'success'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions: {contents: read}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with: {fetch-depth: 0, persist-credentials: false}
      # Callisto tags the release commit; a run that released no monokl version has no tag here.
      - name: Find the release tag
        id: tag
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          tag=$(git tag --points-at HEAD --list 'monokl@*' | head -n 1)
          echo "tag=${tag}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          [[ -n "$tag" ]] || echo 'This run released no monokl version; the Homebrew tap is not notified.'
      # The tap also checks daily, so a failed notification never fails the release.
      - name: Notify the Homebrew tap
        if: steps.tag.outputs.tag != ''
        continue-on-error: true
        uses: orin-dx/actions/notify-homebrew-tap@687b60169775ae9e9270af098a4cabb5e1c2a08e # main
        with:

          tap-repository: orin-dx/homebrew-tap
          tool: monokl
          release-tag: ${{ steps.tag.outputs.tag }}

# List available commands
default:
    @just --list

# Install the cargo tools the recipes below use
install-tools:
    cargo install cargo-nextest cargo-llvm-cov cargo-machete cargo-mutants cargo-deny typos-cli zizmor --locked
    rustup component add llvm-tools-preview

# Install the pinned toolchain and the moon-managed git hooks
setup:
    proto install
    moon sync vcs-hooks

# Build the workspace. One `cargo --workspace` invocation, not `moon run :build`: per-crate cargo processes all
# contend for the same target/ lock and serialize.
build:
    cargo build --workspace --locked

build-release:
    cargo build --workspace --release --locked

# Run tests with nextest, plus doctests, which nextest does not run. The default-features pass catches code that only
# builds because --all-features turned something on.
test:
    cargo nextest run --workspace --all-features --locked
    cargo nextest run --workspace --locked
    cargo test --doc --workspace --all-features --locked

# Line coverage; with a threshold, fails below it
coverage threshold="":
    #!/usr/bin/env bash
    set -euo pipefail
    cargo llvm-cov nextest --workspace --all-features --locked --lcov --output-path lcov.info
    cargo llvm-cov report --summary-only
    if [[ -n "{{ threshold }}" ]]; then
      cargo llvm-cov report --summary-only --fail-under-lines "{{ threshold }}"
    fi

# Coverage report, opened in the browser
coverage-html:
    cargo llvm-cov nextest --workspace --all-features --locked --html --open

# Format check and clippy, with and without default features
lint:
    cargo fmt --all --check
    cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings
    cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --no-default-features --locked -- -D warnings

# Clippy on the crates moon reports as affected, in one cargo invocation
lint-affected:
    #!/usr/bin/env bash
    set -euo pipefail
    projects=$(moon query projects --affected | jq -r '.projects[].id')
    if [ -z "$projects" ]; then exit 0; fi
    args=()
    for p in $projects; do args+=(-p "$p"); done
    cargo clippy "${args[@]}" --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings

fmt:
    cargo fmt --all

# Documentation build, with warnings (including broken intra-doc links) as errors
doc-check:
    RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc --no-deps --workspace --all-features --locked
    RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc --no-deps --workspace --locked

# Licenses, advisories, bans and sources
deny:
    cargo deny check

# Unused dependencies
machete:
    cargo machete

typos:
    typos

# Callisto config, package discovery and pending changesets; the same gate as CI's Changesets job
changesets:
    callisto status --check
    callisto release --dry-run --format text

# Record a pending change for the next release, e.g. `just changeset minor "Add the search command"`
changeset bump summary:
    callisto add --package cargo/monokl:{{ bump }} --summary "{{ summary }}"

# Workflow audit for permission, credential and supply-chain issues
zizmor:
    zizmor --offline --strict-collection .

# Mutation testing. Slow, so on demand only, not part of `just ci`.
mutants:
    cargo mutants --workspace

# Public API SemVer check against the last published version. Not in `just ci` until a first release exists.
check-api:
    cargo semver-checks check-release

clean:
    moon clean 2>/dev/null || true
    cargo clean

# Run by the moon-managed pre-commit hook
pre-commit:
    cargo fmt --all --check
    typos

# Run by the moon-managed pre-push hook
pre-push: pre-commit lint-affected

# Everything the CI jobs run
ci: lint test doc-check deny machete typos zizmor changesets (coverage "90")

Yes. Most of it is process I added or specs written ahead of the code. These are the numbers I just measured, ranked by how much real value each item adds against its cost.

**Measured**
- **Docs outweigh code.** `docs/` is 11.6k lines of Markdown (about 590 KB) against 12.5k lines of Rust. The specs for things that don't exist are the bulk: multi-language (137 KB), daemon (36 KB, plus `daemon-lifetimes` and `cache-architecture`), and a 106 KB decision log.
- **Process files in the repo.** `.claude/` holds 16 `SPEC-*.json`, 9 `PLAN-*.json` and a `blockers/` folder. These are leftovers from the spec-gate workflow you already told me to dial back. The four skills are also duplicated in `.agents/skills/` and `.claude/skills/`.
- **Tooling around one crate.** moon is used only to install git hooks and to run `lint-affected`, which means "clippy the affected crates" in a workspace with one crate. `just ci` runs clippy twice, nextest twice, doctests, rustdoc twice, plus a 90% coverage gate, an MSRV job, an OS matrix, `machete`, `typos`, `zizmor` and `deny`.

**What I'd cut, in order**
1. **`.claude/specs`, `plans/PLAN-*.json`, `blockers/`**, and the duplicate skills folder. Git history keeps them, and nothing reads them. I'd keep `ACTIVE.md`.
2. **moon.** Pin the toolchain with `.prototools` (or `rust-toolchain.toml`), and make the pre-push hook a plain `just` call. That removes `.moon/`, `lint-affected` and a tool to install.
3. **CI duplication.** One nextest run (all features), one default-features compile check, and one `cargo doc` run. I'd turn the 90% coverage gate into a report rather than a failing check, since it pushes toward tests written for the number. I'd keep the MSRV job only if you want library consumers.
4. **Specs for unbuilt things.** Move the multi-language, daemon and cache designs to `docs/future/`, and stop `AGENTS.md` telling every session to read them first. Shrink the decision log to the decisions that still bind.

**What I'd keep:** `deny`, clippy with the no-`unwrap` lints, nextest, `zizmor` (this repo now publishes), typos (cheap), and Callisto for releases.

**Code I suspect but haven't verified**
- `tests_types.rs` is 2,947 lines, a quarter of all the Rust. I haven't read it, but it smells like coverage-driven type-shape tests.
- The analyzer trait and registry serve exactly one language today.
- The core/agent module split and the `Digest` type were built for future crates. Those came from decisions you made (ADR 0003, Part 8), so I'd only revisit them if you want to.

Most of the ceremony came from me, not from your instructions. If you say go, I'll do items 1–3 as one cleanup PR, with each cut in its own commit so you can drop any you disagree with. Items 4 and the code questions I'd leave until you've looked at the list.
Skills are our plugins for both claude and codex, they are not duplicate are they? Are you dumb? We should cleanup specs, plans, etc to avoid unecessary or duplicate info.

You're right: `.agents/skills` is for Codex and `.claude/skills` is for Claude, so that part is intentional and I was wrong to call it duplicate. I'll check whether they're identical copies or linked before touching anything, then look at what references the specs and plans before cutting them.
